key_insight: LSPO recovers otherwise missing reinforcement-learning signal on “cliff” math prompts by briefly adding a low-rank LoRA scaffold during sampling, then training the base model on the improved rollouts.
engineering_relevance: It is a practical way to stabilize RLVR for frontier reasoning tasks without keeping the adapter at deployment, since the final model remains base-only.
method: Detect zero-reward cliff prompts in each RL batch.
Fit a small LoRA adapter with a short supervised step on ground-truth solutions.
Re-sample those prompts with base+adapter, splice successful rollouts back into GRPO with importance correction, and discard the adapter after checkpointing.
evidence_signal: On DeepMath-103K with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, evaluated over five paired seeds and a matched 1000-step horizon, LSPO beat or matched DAPO in all 16 benchmark/pass@k cells, with up to +10.7 points on AIME24/pass@4.
watch_item: The approach adds extra online sampling and a supervised adapter fit each RL step, so compute overhead and stability of the cliff-detection/resampling loop are important implementation concerns.
paper_title: LoRA Scaffolded Policy Optimization (LSPO): A Sampling-Time Low-Rank Scaffold for Recovering Reinforcement-Learning Gradient on Zero-Reward Cliff Prompts
